items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: I'd lost count of the number of rejection letters I'd received. I had long since run out of money and had been sleeping in the office for some time.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: That was my last day at the institute.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: It's hard to say what the final straw was. Maybe it was my last coin dropping down through the sewer grate or the ink freezing because I added too much water to it.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: Or maybe because there wasn't a publisher left that I hadn't tried to contact.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: Regardless, there came a time when I decided that if I got one more rejection letter, I'd leave that place for good.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: I waited and waited. You know, silence is its own message.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: *sigh*
Windsong leans her elbows on the table. The room still smells of mold and damp.
She gets to her feet—there's really nothing better to do anyway. She paces around the room, and as she passes the notice board, a wave of worry washes over her. What is she going to do with it?
Is Ekaterina here? I have a letter for her!
The mailman's voice rings from outside the door. Windsong's heart sinks.
She doesn't move, reluctant to see the contents of the letter. It is slid through the gap under the door.
She picks it up and opens it, just as she has done hundreds of times before.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: "Thank you for submitting ... We regret to inform you ... Best regards."

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: No need to read the rest.
She examines the ink; it's clear it comes from a high-quality printing machine.
She already has a huge pile of letters of the same quality.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: This place is nothing but a ghost town—the shadow of a great era.
A sudden rage boils up in her chest. She smashes the letter onto the board.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: So this is it!
She strides back to her table and whips out the rest of the letters.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: This is where it dies!
"Bam!" She slams another.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: "The 21st century belongs to the study of ley lines!" Come out and say it to my face, you traitor!
"Bam!"

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: All that boasting about "ley lines and quantum physics" ...

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: "Hot springs" ...

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: ... and "the great Ocean Project"!
Her rejection letters now cover the entire board, completely hiding the bulletins announcing those once glorious projects.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: You should be the one to swallow this bitter pill! These rejection letters should've been yours, not mine!
But it is her name that is written on every letter.
Exhausted, she collapses to the floor.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: Not mine ...
Tears well in her eyes and fall on the paper in her hand.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: All us researchers—all the people dedicated to the study of ley lines—put so much time and effort into our work. And now we're all forced to either move on or starve to death.
She tightly grips the letters in her fist, along with the two addressed to Old Nikolas.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: If we hadn't had people who were willing to attend social events and academic meetings, we never would've gained respect in academia. But now they're all in jail, and our reputation is utterly ruined.
She looks around at the dilapidated office. It's nothing like those once bustling and prosperous days.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: We're certainly not the only discipline controlled by bullies and scholars undeserving of their status. So why were we the only discipline to be brought down by this?

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: Because ...

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: *bitter smile*
It's too cruel to say it.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: Neither the people who bury themselves in research nor the people who popularize it can save it.
She sits on the floor, her palm still throbbing from being slammed against the bulletin board.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: Then how am I going to turn the tide?
For a long time, she just sits there, paying no attention to the mold on the floor or the ruptured floor boards.
She hates to just leave. But what else can she do?
She looks up at the notice board that is now towering over her.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: Let the study of ley lines end here, in this cold pit, to die with my career.
She stares at it until her eyes are completely dry, unable to shed any more tears.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: I can't do this anymore.
As the light in the room dims, she drifts into sleep.
"Ring—"

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: Hmm?
"Ring—"
She quickly scrambles to her feet.
"Ring—"
She isn't dreaming. It's the telephone ringing.
She wipes her face on her sleeves and picks up the phone.
Hello. Is that Ms. Ekaterina?

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: It's me. Who's calling? Is that the editor?
She holds the phone tight against her ear, not wanting to miss a single word.
No, this is Sofia.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: Sofia?
Her memories of Yakutsk come rushing back.

items.speaker: Sofia
items.text: Yes, it's me. Now that the weather's warming up in Yakutsk, would you like to come back and continue our research?

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: Research?
She looks around the office. The mold has crept its way to the center of the ceiling.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: Have ... Have you heard about what happened here?
She asks the same question that Yelena and Alexei asked her on that fateful day.

items.speaker: Sofia
items.text: A little bit here and there. I've also heard you've had a tough time getting your paper published. I'm in a bit of a jam here—there's too much work for one person. Would you like to come and lend a hand?

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: But, the study of ley lines has been ...

items.speaker: Sofia
items.text: Whatever happened, does it matter now?
After several moments of painful internal struggle, Windsong speaks again.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: Your research might be disregarded if they find out you're working with a ley hunter.

items.speaker: Sofia
items.text: It's still better than stopping altogether. There are critters' lives at stake.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: I-I'm not sure about this.

items.speaker: Sofia
items.text: You can figure the rest out when you're here, Comrade Ekaterina.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: Aren't you worried about what people might say?

items.speaker: Sofia
items.text: They've got nothing to do with our study, Comrade Ekaterina. You should focus on a more compelling subject.
Sofia's determined tone surprises her.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: Sofia, you ...
"You should focus on a more compelling subject."
She feels a bitter sorrow in her throat.
She holds the receiver tightly in her hands, as if she's holding her dear friend.
For a moment, a genuine fear grips her. What if all this is just a dream?
Tears well in her eyes again. They drop on the desk top and glisten like the morning frost.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: You are right. We ... We should meet in Yakutsk.
Her fingers ache from the clenching, but she is determined not to let go.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: Yakutsk. I can't wait to go back.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: I have to pull the study of ley lines out of this cold grave.

items.speaker: Windsong
items.text: I won't let it die like this.
Once again, she looks at the notice board.
Her heart feels lighter. Finally, there is a new path before her.
